items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: What two millennia of transmitting a canon with no living author, no writing and an active schism left behind — seven copy-integrity mechanisms with engineering forms, offered to any retrieval system that must hand a machine reader something checkable; and the finding that what the transmission left was divergence made detectable, never divergence prevented. A retrieval system that serves text to a machine reader has a problem the machine reader cannot solve for itself: the reader cannot tell a faithful copy from a plausible one. Provenance-Carrying Retrieval argued that the response should therefore carry the means of its own falsification — a hash, an independent time anchor, a citable identifier — and that the trust burden should be inverted, so that a server ships the tools to disbelieve it. This paper asks a different and prior question. Has anything ever actually run this problem to completion? One thing has, and it is not a computer system. The Theravāda Pāli canon was transmitted for roughly four centuries with no written copy at all, and for roughly two millennia in total, without a living author to arbitrate, across schism — on the Sri Lankan chronicles' account, one that produced a rival recital — through famine, war, and the ordinary attrition of the human beings who were the storage medium. That is a copy-integrity problem under a threat model that overlaps a retrieval server's without being the same one (§7 partitions the two), sustained for a duration no production system has approached. It converged on an apparatus, and this paper reads seven of its parts as engineering. All seven are transpositions, and the paper says so plainly. Five transpose practices the archival and transparency-log communities already know under other names: an inline attribution formula opening the text rather than a metadata field (§4.1); admission decided at build time by a named assembly under a recorded procedure rather than by a query-time filter (§4.2); commentary labelled as a distinct text class , from which a server inherits an obligation never to substitute generated summary for source (§4.3); variant readings preserved with their line of transmission attached rather than normalised to a preferred text (§4.4); and abridgement announced inline at the point of the cut (§4.5). Two more transpose practices known in other fields: interpretive standing carried per passage rather than per document, because an excerpt loses its document's front matter at retrieval (§4.6); and scheduled public re-verification before an assembly in which silence is a positive assertion for which the silent party is accountable (§4.7). An eighth item is a convention rather than a mechanism — every exclusion served with the case that occasioned it (§4.8). Two further designs (§5) are carried furthest from where the destination field keeps them. The conformance endpoint (§5.1) accepts a claimed quotation and returns a disposition on the claim , together with the procedure to follow next, and by construction returns no disposition on the claimant — the part a hash does not have, because a hash reports that a comparison failed and says nothing about what to do. It is offered as a new composition: closed disposition sets about a submitted object are old (OCSP), and what is new is a set over a multi-recension corpus that includes a conforming variant with its witness. The separated completeness manifest (§5.2) is a signed, versioned and expiring statement of a collection's membership and cardinality published as an artifact distinct from the index it describes, on the ground that an index cannot attest to its own completeness : a silently dropped document is invisible to every check that reads the index, and detectable to a third party holding only the manifest. It is a transposition, with The Update Framework's snapshot and timestamp metadata and BagIt's Payload-Oxum as its nearest prior art. items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.

items.summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.

items.summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: Conventional capillary heat pipes route vapor and returning condensate through the same envelope, so the two streams interact along the entire transport length. This work reports a D-shaped two-phase loop that separates the two paths geometrically: a wicked vertical leg carries evaporation and vapor transport, and a curved copper return leg carries condensate back to a submerged reservoir at the base of the vertical leg, which acts as a hydrostatic trap that excludes vapor from the return path. Three additively manufactured triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) wicks of a common fill-ratio class and unit-cell size were tested in this envelope, gyroid, Schwarz Diamond, and Schwarz Primitive, together with a conventional copper-mesh heat pipe as benchmark. Devices were operated vertically at measured heater powers of 30.3, 40.5, and 50.8 W. Schwarz Diamond and gyroid gave the lowest power-averaged thermal resistance of the four configurations, reaching 1.70 and 1.69 ÅãC/W at 50.8W and holding the evaporator 23.7 and 20.1 ÅãC cooler than the benchmark at that power. Extrapolating the measured resistance to a length-scaled maximum heat-transport capability, Schwarz Diamond and gyroid exceed the copper-mesh benchmark by approximately 9% and 6% at the tested 0.30m length; these are single-run, architecture-level comparisons and are not repeated-trial estimates. Within this matched-class triplet, porosity identifies which structures form the leading pair while simulated single-phase permeability predicts the reverse ordering. Porosity is therefore the more reliable near-term predictor of thermal performance among architected lattices tested at a fixed fill-ratio class, though the device comparisons were not repeated and porosity remains one of several confounded structural parameters.
items.title: Porosity versus Permeability as Predictors of Thermal Performance in Architected TPMS Wicks for a D-Shaped Separated-Flow Heat Pipe

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. Companion to the five-essay Spine. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.

items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a Structured PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22737224 . Does the introduction explain the objective of the research presented in the preprint? Yes It explains the problem properly, namely the need for reliable methods for miRNA analysis, as RNA-seq methods are not able to account for its specific characteristics. It also points out the gaps in prior benchmarking studies, clearly identifying that a benchmark particularly for normalization and differential expression has not been performed before, especially one incorporating recently developed methods. Lastly, it clearly states its aim and overall approach. Are the methods well-suited for this research? Somewhat appropriate 1. Some methodological details are missing. PCA and heatmap figures (figure 1B and 1C) are presented in Results alone, with no explanation in Methods section. So no information on the input data (raw or normalized or log), if it was scaled, the miRNAs selection criteria, or what clustering methods were applied. Due to this, the reproducibility of the paper is affected. 2. The paper frames as evaluating a broad range of normalization strategies but just tests only two types: within-sample scaling (RPM, RPM_total, MAP) and cross-sample (DESeq2,TMM). Other options such as quantile normalization or compositional data methods were not tested. 3. An uneven comparison in the differential expression benchmark, two different input data types used. Most methods use miRNA-level count matrix whereas miRglmm uses isomiR-level count matrix. Still, the authors do not address whether miRglmm's strong performance is due to the model or input data. 4. The underlying logic for the ground truth is circular. The authors state that DE ground truth is defined by "monotonicity trends derived from RPM values". But RPM is what they recommend for normalization. So ranking other tools against a baseline that uses their preferred method creates a feedback loop that is not validated against any independent benchmark. Are the conclusions supported by the data? Somewhat supported 1. The paper relies almost entirely on monotonicity as the ground-truth signal, across normalization, differential expression and log2FC tissue-specificity direction. While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. The authors identified pancreatic contamination in Mouse 3, clearly separating on PC2. They state that removing Mouse 3 did not alter the normalization or DE benchmarking results, but it is based only on supplementary figures and not present in the main text. So, it can not be independently verified. 3. items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: Reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript "When Data Substitution Changes the Scientific Question: Claim-Level Evidence Admissibility in Wildfire Robustness Analysis." This archive supports the claim-specific continuity test through the benchmark and release-contract registries, registered semantic coding, SOCR schema and examples, verification code, conformance and metamorphic tests, rule-to-record checks, and the blinded semantic-coding packet. Deterministic verification is conditional on the registered semantic coding. Independent semantic-coding reliability was not evaluated. The archive does not establish external validation. items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .
items.title: The Cost of Reliability in Optimal Magnetization Switching: A Longitudinal-Field Front for Van der Waals Magnets

items.summary: This record contains the frozen computational data and source code supporting the study “Production Capacity Is Not Growth Coupling: Exhaustive Analysis of PHB Strain Designs.” The archive includes the curated iJA1121 M1 model of Priestia megaterium DSM319; complete growth-optimal classifications for the defined 59-reaction, one- to four-knockout space across four aerobic carbon conditions; zero-product certificates; the C1 same-vector epsilon-capacity oracle and Pareto products; the seed-10–29 active-learning replication; the 280,000-record capacity-surrogate and target-specific SHAP re-execution; bounded genome-scale constrained-minimal-cut-set results; configuration files; registration and amendment documents; solver audits; software environments; and SHA-256 manifests. All reported outcomes are in silico properties of the frozen model, bounds, intervention universe, and numerical tolerances.
items.title: PHB Growth-Coupling Classification and Capacity-Oracle Benchmark for the Curated iJA1121 M1 Model of Priestia megaterium DSM319
